newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore firms sign deals with Hungary.
newsitem.headline: Singapore firms sign deals with Hungary.

text.p: Singapore and Hungarian firms signed three commercial agreements on Thursday, a Singapore Trade Development Board statement said.
The agreements were signed during a Singapore-Hungary business forum and witnessed by visiting Hungarian Prime Minister Gyula Horn.
They included an acquisition deal between trading-based Thakral Group and Hungary's Yuganskorionneftegaz Kft.
Under the agreement, Thakral acquired 77 percent of the Hungarian firm, which makes consumer and telecommunications products.
Thakral will invest US$7 million in the Hungarian company, which had sales of US$10 million in 1996.
Thakral already has a distribution network in Eastern Europe and the acquisition will further enhance its presence there, a Thakral official said.
Another agreement, between Royal Selangor (S) Pte Ltd and Herend Porcelain Manufactory Ltd, was for a joint venture to set up boutiques to sell Hungarian porcelain in Southeast Asia.
The Singapore Conferdation of Industries and the Federation of Hungarian Industrialists also signed an agreement to promote businesses between the two countries.
The Trade Development Board said Singapore's investments in Hungary, totalling more than Singapore $30 million (US$21 million), are concentrated in the manufacturing and hospitality industries.
This included the Government Investment Corporation of Singapore investing seven percent in a multiplex cinema.
Bilateral trade between Hungary and Singapore was S$125 million in 1996, up 50 percent from 1995.
Horn was in Singapore on a visit to boost trade and investment, the first call on Singapore by a Hungarian prime minister. He leaves the city-state on Saturday.
During the visit the two countries will sign agreements to guarantee investments and avoid double taxation.
